I was promised a job as a member of a software development team being put together to work on a brand new Java software platform.

I turned up on the first day to find that the "team" I was working with all belonged to an out-sourcing company from Mumbai, and my boss and project manager were in a completely different state, so I was all alone.

I then found out that this brand new software platform was actually just a re-branding of an existing software platform, which was already very old, extremely over-engineered and completely bug-ridden. All of the original developers had long since left, so nobody actually understood how any of it worked any more, and nobody could figure it out because the code was such a horrible, overly complex mess. The normal Java development environments couldn't even open the project without spewing thousands of errors; it had to be built from an equally over-engineered Maven build script that took over an hour to run and had somehow managed to break incremental builds (meaning that it would rebuild the entire thing from scratch even if you only changed a single line of source code). It was Java-enterprise-hell taken to another level!

Now I've worked on some complex code-bases before and I've solved some very difficult software engineering problems, but I could barely even complete the most basic of assignments on this project. My manager (who was also new to the project) thought I was just a bad hire and so started giving me small, shitty tasks. I did that for another 6 months before I eventually quit too. I'm pretty sure that project will be dead by now, or if it's not (unfortunately quite a lot of other projects were actually using it internally), it'll be slowly marching on with a huge developer turn-over rate.

I go back and forth on this issue, but it always comes back to the fact of whether or not I believe laws such as the above are doing more harm than good.

The sad fact of the matter is, you will always be what your genes have dictated you will be. And yes, you can sign pieces of paper and have surgery to tell people otherwise, but...

I guess I'll never really understand unless I suffered from gender dysphoria, anymore than I would understand what it would be like for suffers of any other number of cognitive disorders, though I will never buy into the whole idea that gender and sex are somehow mutually exclusive.

There will always be the bad and the good.

The Ireland law has restrictions for people age 16-18, who are likely to make decisions about their gender that may not be certain. Hopefully, they don't decide to make this age any younger. There will always be irresponsible adults as well.

I disagree with surgery requirements to get legal gender changed, which is the main requirement that this law has changed. Before, you had to get either a sex change surgery or some other sort of surgery in order to get legally recognized as your gender. Many trans people do not choose to get surgery and pass just fine without it.
